title: Map skills
examples: How do I know which way is north on this map?
What does the scale on the map actually mean?
Can you show me how to use the symbols key?

explain.say: Today we are learning important map skills for reading maps. We will look at the compass, scale, and symbols. These tools help us understand any map.
The compass on a map shows the four main directions. North, south, east, and west are the main points. Always remember that north is usually at the top.

draw.text: Cardinal Directions: N, S, E, W

explain.say: The scale tells us the distance on the map compared to real life. For example, one centimeter might equal ten kilometers in reality. This helps you measure real distances.

draw.text: Scale: Map distance to real distance

explain.say: Symbols are pictures on the map that stand for real things. A small drawing of a church means a place of worship. Always check the map key for what symbols mean.

faq.q: What is the difference between the compass and the key?
faq.a: The compass shows the directions like north and south. The key, or legend, explains what the symbols on the map mean.
asks: What does the map key do?
How do I know which way is up?

faq.q: If the scale is one inch to one mile, how do I use it?
faq.a: You can use a ruler to measure the distance between two points on the map. Then, you multiply that measurement by the scale factor.
asks: How do I measure distance on a map?
What does the scale tell me?

faq.q: Do all maps use the same symbols?
faq.a: No, different maps use different symbols. You must always look at the map's key to know what each symbol represents.
asks: Do I need a key for every map?

faq.q: If I travel east on a map, am I going in the opposite direction of west?
faq.a: Yes, east and west are opposite directions on the compass rose. They are separated by the north and south lines.
asks: What is the opposite of east?
How do I find opposite directions?

faq.q: Is the compass always pointing to true north?
faq.a: Most school maps use a simplified compass rose showing the main points. Always check if the map mentions magnetic or true north.

facts: The compass points show the four main directions: north, south, east, and west.
The scale compares a distance on the map to a real-life distance.
The map key or legend explains the meaning of the symbols used.
Cardinal directions are the four main points on a compass.

quiz.say: If the scale is one centimeter to fifty kilometers, and two points are ten centimeters apart, what is the real distance?
quiz.why: You multiply the map distance by the scale factor to find the real distance.

wrong.1: This mistake happens if you only use the number one from the scale.
wrong.2: This mistake happens if you multiply the numbers incorrectly.
wrong.3: This mistake happens if you forget to use the scale entirely.

quiz.say: If a map symbol shows a drawing of a cross, what does the map key most likely tell you?
quiz.why: The map key tells you that the symbol of a cross represents a place of worship.

wrong.0: Tree symbols are usually different from religious symbols.
wrong.2: A crossroads is usually shown by intersecting roads, not a cross symbol.
wrong.3: This is too general; the key gives a specific meaning.

quiz.say: If you are facing east on a map, which direction is directly behind you?
quiz.why: West is the exact opposite direction from east on a compass.

wrong.1: North is perpendicular to east, not directly opposite.
wrong.2: South is also perpendicular to east, not directly opposite.
wrong.3: You cannot be facing the same direction and its opposite at the same time.
